core_obligations: Reduction to a presheaf computation (proof lines 8463-8473): the limit of a finite diagram of sheaves is computed as a presheaf and is the limit in the category of sheaves, so it suffices to compare the stalk of that presheaf with the limit of the stalks.

Interchange (proof lines 8473-8481): using the explicit description of the presheaf limit and of the stalk, the assertion becomes the commutation of a limit with the colimit over the neighbourhoods, which holds because the opposite of the category of neighbourhoods is filtered by assumption.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the statement to a presheaf computation.
Apply the commutation of filtered colimits with finite limits.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a functor whose category of neighbourhoods is cofiltered the associated stalk functor is left exact (statement lines 8454-8460). The proof is a complete computation: the limit of a finite diagram of sheaves is computed as a presheaf and is the limit in the category of sheaves (proof lines 8463-8469); the assertion is then rewritten using the explicit descriptions of the presheaf limit and of the stalk (proof lines 8470-8477); and the resulting commutation of a limit with the colimit over the neighbourhoods holds because the opposite category of neighbourhoods is filtered (proof lines 8479-8481). The non-formal content is the rewriting and the filteredness input. The claim is H2: a structured computation with each input named.
